Main.sentence: The Norwegian Nobel Committee ( ___E:Norwegian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_language)___ : Den norske Nobelkomité ) selects the recipients of the ___E:Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ each year on behalf of Swedish industrialist ___E:Alfred Nobel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel)___ 's ___E:estate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estate_(law))___ , based on instructions of Nobel's ___E:will U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_(law))___ .
Five members are appointed by the ___E:Norwegian Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Parliament)___ .
In his will, ___E:Alfred Nobel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel)___ tasked the parliament of Norway with selecting the winners of the Nobel Peace Prize.
At the time, Norway and ___E:Sweden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden)___ were in ___E:a loose personal union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_between_Sweden_and_Norway)___ .
Despite its members being appointed by Parliament, the committee is a private body tasked with awarding a private prize.
In recent decades, most committee members were retired politicians.
The committee is assisted by its secretariat, the ___E:Norwegian Nobel Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Institute)___ .
The committee holds their meetings in the institute's building, where the winner is also announced.
Since 1990, however, the award ceremony takes place in ___E:Oslo City Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oslo_City_Hall)___ .
___E:Alfred Nobel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel)___ died in December 1896. In January 1897 the contents of his ___E:will U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_(law))___ were unveiled.

It was written as early as in 1895.  He declared that a ___E:Nobel Peace Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize)___ should be awarded "to the person who shall have done the most or the best work for fraternity between nations, for the abolition or reduction of standing armies and for the holding and promotion of peace congresses",  and that some of Nobel's money was to be donated to this prize.
The ___E:Nobel Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation)___ manages the assets.

The other ___E:Nobel Prizes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize)___ were to be awarded by Swedish bodies ( ___E:Swedish Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_Academy)___ , ___E:Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences)___ , ___E:Karolinska Institutet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karolinska_Institute)___ ) that already existed, whereas the responsibility for the Peace Prize was given to the ___E:Norwegian Parliament U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storting)___ ,  specifically "a committee of five persons to be elected" by it.  A new body had to be created—the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

Jurist ___E:Fredrik Heffermehl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fredrik_Heffermehl)___ has noted that a legislative body could not necessarily be expected to handle a judicial task like managing a legal will. The task of a parliament is to create and change laws whereas a will can not be changed unless the premises are clearly outdated.

However, this question was not debated in depth, out of contemporary fear that the donated money might be lost in legal battles if the body was not created soon.  On 26 April 1897 the Norwegian Parliament accepted the assignment and on 5 August the same year it formalized the process of election and service time for committee members.

The first Peace Prize was awarded in 1901 to ___E:Henri Dunant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_Dunant)___ and ___E:Frédéric Passy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%A9d%C3%A9ric_Passy)___ .
In the beginning, the committee was filled with active parliamentarians and the annual reports were discussed in parliamentary sessions.
These ties to the Norwegian Parliament were later weakened so that the committee became more independent.

Accordingly, the name was changed from the Norwegian Nobel Committee to the Nobel Committee of the Norwegian Parliament ( ___E:Norwegian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_language)___ : Det norske Stortings Nobelkomité ) in 1901, but changed back in 1977.  Now, active parliamentarians cannot sit on the committee, unless they have explicitly stated their intent to step down shortly.
Nonetheless, the committee is still composed mainly of politicians.
A 1903 proposition to elect a law scholar ( ___E:Ebbe Hertzberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ebbe_Hertzberg)___ ) was rejected.

In late 1948, the election system was changed to make the committee more proportional with parliamentary representation of ___E:Norwegian political parties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Norway)___ .
The Norwegian Labour Party, which controlled a simple majority of seats in the Norwegian Parliament orchestrated this change.
This practice has been cemented, but sharply criticized.
There have been propositions about including non-Norwegian members in the committee, but this has never happened.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee is assisted by the ___E:Norwegian Nobel Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Institute)___ , established in 1904.  The committee might receive well more than a hundred nominations and asks the Nobel Institute in February every year to research about twenty candidates.
The director of the Nobel Institute also serves as secretary to the Norwegian Nobel Committee; currently this position belongs to Olav Njølstad.

In January 1944 an attempt by the ___E:Quisling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidkun_Quisling)___ government to take over the functions of the Nobel Committee led to the resignation of Jahn and other committee members.

The Swedish ___E:consulate-general U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consulate-general)___ in Oslo formally took over the management of the Foundation's Oslo property on behalf of the Nobel Foundation.

The committee is assisted by the ___E:Norwegian Nobel Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Nobel_Institute)___ , its secretariat.
The leader of the institute holds the title secretary.
The secretary is not a member of the committee, but is an employee of the Norwegian Nobel Institute.
